litematica_printer.config.breakBlocksPer:
Number of blocks that can be broken per game tick. Higher values mean more blocks broken each time (provided the blocks can be broken within one game tick).
Set to §b0§r for no limit, you can try enabling §6§lUse Packet Placement§r to optimize efficiency.
litematica_printer.config.breakCheckHard: Whether to skip unbreakable blocks (blocks with hardness of -1). If only the hardness of certain blocks has been modified on the server side, you can disable this option.
litematica_printer.config.breakVeilToggl:
When enabled (requires Packet Mining), blocks in the Veil List skip hardness and server checks, directly sending the start-destroy and stop-destroy packets within the same game tick for instant breaking. Respects the mining interval and blocks-per-tick limits.
§l§cNOTE:§r Make sure the server allows this.
Only blocks in this list trigger the "send start-destroy and stop-destroy in the same tick" veil logic. An empty list means all blocks trigger it. Supports item IDs, simplified IDs (without minecraft:), and item names; pinyin and tags are supported.
Cooldown time after breaking blocks at the same location (in game ticks). Retry breaking operation only after cooldown ends.
Interval time for breaking blocks (in game ticks).
Set to 0 for no interval (may cause server lag), recommended to set to 1-5 to balance speed and performance.

litematica_printer.config.breakBlacklist:
Prohibit mining blocks in this list.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.

Block filtering rules for mining mode.
§dNo Limit§r: No restriction on any block mining
§dWhitelist§r: Only allow mining blocks in whitelist
§dBlacklist§r: Prohibit mining blocks in blacklist
§lNote:§r When using Tweakeroo mining limit presets, this setting will not take effect.§r
litematica_printer.config.breakLimiter.d:
Source of mining limit rules:
§dTweakeroo Preset§r: Use Tweakeroo mod's mining limit rules
§dCustom§r: Use printer's custom mining limit rules.
litematica_printer.config.breakProgressT:
Progress threshold when mining blocks. Mining is considered complete when this percentage is reached.
Higher values mean lower mining efficiency; lower values mean faster mining efficiency.
Since the break progress reaches 70% after the first game tick, then wait for end mining packet reception,
you can lower it on servers without additional mining detection. :)
litematica_printer.config.breakUsePacket: Use sending mining packets instead of conventional mining logic, which can theoretically speed up mining efficiency.
litematica_printer.config.breakSound.des: Controls local breaking sounds for printer block breaking, regardless of packet mining.
litematica_printer.config.breakWhitelist:
Only allow mining blocks in this list.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Input text and filter conditions simultaneously (separated by English comma), example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.

litematica_printer.config.checkPlayerInt:
When enabled, printer only processes blocks within player's block interaction range.
Positions beyond interaction distance will not perform operations to avoid cross-distance operations being detected by servers.
If you're playing on servers that allow cross-distance interaction, you can disable this option.
litematica_printer.config.closeAllMode.d: Close all working modes; if currently running in single mode, will automatically revert to printing mode.
litematica_printer.config.handRestockShu: Detects item consumption automatically (hand uses, bow/crossbow arrows, totem pops, etc.): when the main inventory has none of the item left but shulker boxes do, extracts some via Quick Shulker and tries to return it to the slot it was consumed from (skipped if the target slot is occupied). Requires Quick Shulker.
litematica_printer.config.debugOutput.de:
When enabled, console will output printer debug information.
If §6§lShow Work Status§r is also enabled, some information will also be displayed in the operation interface.
litematica_printer.config.refillAmountAd: Adjust Cloud Storage Refill Amount (Hold + Scroll)

Hold this key and scroll the mouse wheel to adjust the "cloud storage refill amount" (shown live above the inventory). Default: scroll up increases, down decreases. Only available when Cloud Storage Mod is loaded.
litematica_printer.config.refillScrollRe: Reverse Cloud Storage Refill Scroll Direction
When enabled, scrolling up decreases and scrolling down increases while holding the adjust key.
litematica_printer.config.easyPlaceProto:
Use Servex's easy place protocol to handle block placement correction during printing.
§lNote:§r This feature only works in single-player or on servers with Servux installed.

litematica_printer.config.fill.desc: Within the selection range, place blocks configured in §6Fill Block List§r.
Block list used by filling mode, configuration rules consistent with "Basic Block List".
Block selection mode for filling.
§dBlock List§r: Use blocks in configured list
§dHeld Item§r: Use currently held block in main hand
litematica_printer.config.fillModeFacing: Facing settings when filling blocks. For example, placing upper slabs or lower slabs.
litematica_printer.config.fillSelectionT:
Working selection range rules for filling mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute filling within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection
litematica_printer.config.fluid.desc: At lava sources and water sources positions, default place blocks configured in §6Fluid Replacement Block List§r.
litematica_printer.config.fluidList.desc: List of liquids that need to be replaced, can only input liquid IDs, example: §bminecraft:water§r.
litematica_printer.config.fluidModeFillF: When enabled, flowing liquids will also be treated as targets needing filling and replacement.
litematica_printer.config.fluidReplaceBl:
Block list for filling liquids. Can input item ID or displayed name, example: §bminecraft:sand§r §bsand§r.

§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute fluid removal within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection
litematica_printer.config.mine.desc: Mine all non-liquid blocks within selection range.
litematica_printer.config.mineSelectionT:
Working selection range rules for mining mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute mining within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection (default)
litematica_printer.config.modeSwitch.des:
§dSingle Mode§r: Only run one working mode at a time
§dMulti Mode§r: Can run multiple working modes simultaneously
§lNote:§r Need to reopen settings menu after switching to see mode change effects.§r
litematica_printer.config.multiBreak.des: When enabled, execute operations according to mode priority. Low priority modes will pause when high priority modes are running.
litematica_printer.config.openScreen.des: Hotkey to open printer settings menu (the page you're currently viewing).
litematica_printer.config.placeBlocksPer:
Number of blocks that can be placed per game tick. Higher values mean more blocks placed each time.
Set to §b0§r for no limit. On servers with packet restrictions, you can try enabling §6§lUse Packet Placement§r to optimize efficiency.
litematica_printer.config.placeSameItemF: Keep placing targets that use the current block item before switching to another item.
litematica_printer.config.itemSwitchInte: Ticks to wait before switching to another placement item.
Cooldown time after processing a block at the same location (in game ticks). Retry placement operation only after cooldown ends.
litematica_printer.config.placeInAir.des: Ignore block support requirements and place blocks directly in air positions (applicable to unsupported decorative blocks).
Interval time for placing blocks (in game ticks).
May automatically add delays to avoid placement errors for some special blocks.
Setting to 0 may cause poor performance on servers with packet restrictions.
Not recommended to set to 0 when printing redstone mechanisms.
litematica_printer.config.placeUsePacket:
Use sending placement packets instead of conventional placement logic to reduce "ghost block" phenomenon.
Can try enabling this in environments with packet restrictions.
litematica_printer.config.printSound.des: Controls local placement sounds for printer block placement, regardless of packet printing.
litematica_printer.config.printAutoFillC:
Automatically fill compostable items into composters to generate bone meal.
(§lWarning: This operation will consume compostable items in inventory!§r)

Compostable items used for automatic composter filling.
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:wheat§r §bwheat§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#compostable§r.
Add ",c" after text for contains matching (prioritizing pinyin/direct matching), example: §lwheat,c§r.
litematica_printer.config.printBonemealC: Use bone meal to grow crops.
litematica_printer.config.printAutoStrip: When enabled, if stripped logs are not in inventory, will first place normal logs, then automatically strip them with axe to save manual operation time.
litematica_printer.config.printAutoTunin: When printing note blocks, automatically tune note blocks to the pitch specified in schematic.
litematica_printer.config.printBreakExtr: Automatically break extra blocks that don't exist in schematic during printing.
litematica_printer.config.printBreakWron: Automatically break blocks that completely mismatch the schematic during printing.

Automatically break blocks whose type matches schematic but state doesn't, and need to be broken for adjustment during printing.
Examples: stairs/slabs with wrong orientation, vines with extra faces, etc.; blocks that can be corrected by clicking (like trapdoors, campfires) won't be broken.
litematica_printer.config.printFallingBl: When enabled, will check if blocks below falling blocks match schematic, and skip placement if incorrect.
litematica_printer.config.printForcedSne: Automatically maintain sneaking state during printing process.
litematica_printer.config.printHotkey.de: When holding the bound hotkey, printer will continuously place blocks.
litematica_printer.config.printFillCauld: When enabled, the printer resolves cauldron mismatches by right-clicking with buckets (lava/powder snow/water/empty bucket) to fill or scoop contents. Cauldrons are never broken as wrong blocks.
litematica_printer.config.printIceForWat: Generate water source blocks through "place ice → break ice" method to achieve water source printing.
litematica_printer.config.printMode.repl:
In replacement mode, replace specified source blocks with target blocks in selection area.
Can input source block ID/name and target block ID/name (separated by English colon), example: §bminecraft:stone:minecraft:oak_planks§r §bstone:oak_planks§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#logs:minecraft:oak_planks§r (replace all logs with oak planks).
litematica_printer.config.printReplace.d: Directly overwrite blocks in list without skipping processing or breaking.
litematica_printer.config.printSubstitut: When enabled, a missing target block can be placed with blocks registered in the Substitute List; the target block itself is always preferred when available. The default list substitutes live coral for dead coral.

One rule per line: 'sub1,sub2,...:target'. Multiple rules can also be separated by ';' within a line. Names strictly match a block's registry path (fire_coral), full ID (minecraft:fire_coral) or exact translated name (e.g. 'Dead Fire Coral'); fuzzy/pinyin search is not used, and a name matching multiple blocks invalidates the rule. With Substitute Placement enabled, missing targets are placed with substitutes in list order; substitute blocks are also exempt from 'Break Wrong Blocks' (wrong states are still corrected).
litematica_printer.config.printReplaceab:
Block list that can be directly overwritten during printing (without breaking original blocks).
Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Add ",c" after text for contains matching, example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
litematica_printer.config.printSafelyObs: Check if suitable for placement before placing observers to avoid accidentally triggering your machines and causing disasters.
litematica_printer.config.printSelection:
Working selection range rules for printing mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute printing within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection (default)
litematica_printer.config.printSkip.desc: When enabled, will skip blocks in the list during printing.
Block list skipped during printing. Can input item ID or translated name in current language, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Add ",c" after text for contains matching, example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
litematica_printer.config.printScanWhite: When enabled and the list is non-empty, printing only scans and places blocks in the list. Verifier-highlighted “missing blocks” are exempt (also scanned and placed). Affects printing only — the auto-walk target filter is the “Pathfinding Scan Whitelist” in the Pathfinding tab. Scan time is still limited by Iteration Time Limit.

Blocks targeted by printing scans when the whitelist is enabled. Same format as Skip Placement - List: item ID or translated name, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Add “,c” for contains matching, example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
litematica_printer.config.printScanAutoW: While printing, scans the schematic in the player’s chunk section (within Work Time Budget) for unplaced blocks and auto-walks you to each target via pathfinding (WASD+Ctrl+Jump only, camera untouched). On arrival it releases control and waits until the block is placed, then walks to the next. With the “Pathfinding Scan Whitelist” off it scans everything (all unplaced blocks are targets); when enabled with a non-empty list, only list-verified or verifier-highlighted blocks are targeted. Sections expand via BFS in x+, x-, z+, z-, y+, y- order.
When enabled, movement no longer walks: you must ride a Happy Ghast and fly in 3D toward pending blocks. The flight space must stay entirely inside schematic-predicted air (outside the schematic, real blocks are still respected), and both the ghast and the rider hitbox must fit. A hint is shown below screen center when not riding / not the first rider / no harness equipped / occupied by a standing player. Prerequisite: "Scan Auto-Walk" must also be enabled, otherwise this feature is fully disabled (only the manual /go command is exempt).
litematica_printer.config.pathNearestTar: When enabled, scan auto-walk runs one multi-goal pathfinding over all candidates and picks the block with the truly shortest walking path (a straight-line-near but far-to-reach target is no longer preferred). When disabled, keeps the old behavior: nearest by straight line + single-goal pathfinding.
litematica_printer.config.goScanExtraBlo: When enabled, scan auto-walk treats "extra blocks" (schematic says air but a block exists in reality) as priority targets: it walks to them first and waits for the printer to break them; multiple extras compete by shortest path. Requires "Break Extra Blocks" to be enabled. Note: with the printer's scan whitelist active, air cells are not whitelisted and extras will not be broken.
litematica_printer.config.goScanWrongBlo: When enabled, scan auto-walk also treats "wrong blocks" (the schematic expects one block here but a different block exists in reality; it must be broken and replaced) as targets. They share the same candidate pool as unplaced blocks and compete by shortest path (no priority dispatch). Requires "Break Wrong Blocks" to be enabled, otherwise the printer will not break-and-replace and walking there just waits forever. Not constrained by the "Pathfinding Target Whitelist" (which only filters unplaced blocks); "wrong state" (same block, mismatched state) is not a target and is corrected by the printer in passing.
litematica_printer.config.pathTargetCand: Upper bound of candidates entering the multi-goal target set (16~1024, default 256). Excess candidates are pre-filtered by straight-line distance — the distance is a pre-filter only; the shortest target is still decided by real path cost. Lower values reduce computation but may miss the true shortest target in extreme detour scenarios.
litematica_printer.config.walkScanWhitel: When enabled and the list is non-empty, scan auto-walk only treats unplaced blocks in the list or highlighted by the verifier as targets and walks you to them. It filters pathfinding targets only — it does not affect the scan itself (the scan always enumerates every block) and does not constrain "Pathfind to Wrong Blocks" or "Pathfind to Extra Blocks", which are gated by their own toggles. Fully independent of the “Scan Whitelist” in the Printing tab.

Blocks treated as unplaced-block targets by scan auto-walk when its whitelist is enabled and non-empty. Same format as Skip Placement - List: item ID or translated name, example: §bminecraft:stone§r §bsandstone§r.
Prefix §b#§r for tag matching, example: §l#minecraft:logs§r.
Add “,c” for contains matching, example: §lglazed_terracotta,c§r.
Union with verifier highlights: selecting the “missing blocks” category (or individual entries) in the verifier makes those blocks walk targets even when absent from the list.
litematica_printer.config.printScanSecti: Axis priority for BFS expansion into adjacent chunk sections; each axis expands + first, then -. Default X→Z→Y = x+, x-, z+, z-, y+, y-.
litematica_printer.config.printScanXReve: When enabled, the X axis expands in the negative direction first.
litematica_printer.config.printScanYReve: When enabled, the Y axis expands in the negative direction first.
litematica_printer.config.printScanZReve: When enabled, the Z axis expands in the negative direction first.
litematica_printer.config.printerAutoDis: Automatically disable printer when player dies to avoid misoperations after respawning.
litematica_printer.config.printerAutoEna: When enabled, the printer is automatically enabled when entering a server. Death and respawning does not trigger it again, and auto-disable on death still works.
litematica_printer.config.printerIterato:
Block iteration order during printing:
§dXYZ§r: X axis first, then Y axis, finally Z axis
§dXZY§r: X axis first, then Z axis, finally Y axis
§dYXZ§r: Y axis first, then X axis, finally Z axis
§dYZX§r: Y axis first, then Z axis, finally X axis
§dZXY§r: Z axis first, then X axis, finally Y axis
§dZYX§r: Z axis first, then Y axis, finally X axis

Area shape for printer block iteration:
§dCube§r: Cube with §6§lWork Radius§r as edge length (recommended value: 3)
§dSphere§r: Sphere with §6§lWork Radius§r as radius (recommended value: 6)
§dOctahedron§r: Octahedron with §6§lWork Radius§r as edge length (recommended value: 6)
litematica_printer.config.printerLagChec: used as the upper limit for lag detection.
litematica_printer.config.printerMode.de:
Printer's core work mode:
§dPrinting§r: Restore blocks in projection blueprint (including direction, state and other properties)
§dMining§r: Mine blocks within selection range (except fluids)
§dBedrock Breaking§r: Break bedrock within selection range using game mechanics (only available for 1.19+ with Bedrock Miner mod installed)
§dFluid Removal§r: Fill liquids in projection selection with specified blocks
§dFilling§r: Fill projection selection with blocks

§lNote:§r Except for §dPrinting§r mode, operation ranges of other modes are all within projection selection, can also be changed by adjusting §6§lSelection Type§r of each mode.
litematica_printer.config.printerSelecti:
Working selection range rules for printing mode:
§dProjection Selection§r: Use complete selection currently selected in projection as working range
§dProjection Render Layer§r: Only execute printing within current render layer range of projection
§dProjection Selection Below Player§r: Only process areas below player's height in selection
§dProjection Selection Above Player§r: Only process areas above player's height in selection
litematica_printer.config.printerWorking:
Number of block operations executed per game tick (only effective when print interval is set to 0).
Recommended to set to 2-8 to balance speed and performance. Too high values may get kicked by server.
litematica_printer.config.printerXAxisRe: When enabled, X axis iteration order changes to largest to smallest.
litematica_printer.config.printerYAxisRe: When enabled, Y axis iteration order changes to largest to smallest.
litematica_printer.config.printerZAxisRe: When enabled, Z axis iteration order changes to largest to smallest.
litematica_printer.config.moveAdaptiveIt: Affects parallel breaking only. When enabled, while moving fast prioritize the axis the player is approaching and put it as the outermost iteration axis, reducing missed blocks (especially along Y) during fast parallel breaking. Does not affect placement or other modes.
litematica_printer.config.motionAheadBlo: Affects parallel breaking only. Extra block layers (in blocks) scanned ahead along the player's dominant movement axis, so newly entered layers are scanned earlier during parallel breaking. 0 disables the extension.
litematica_printer.config.quickShulker.d: Directly take needed materials from shulker boxes in inventory for quick item retrieval.
litematica_printer.config.quickShulkerMa: Maximum number of matching item stacks to take from a shulker box per retrieval, from 1 to 27.
litematica_printer.config.quickShulkerCo: Cooldown time for quick shulker function (in game ticks). Some plugin servers have cooldown restrictions for this function. Set to 0 to disable cooldown.
litematica_printer.config.renderHud.desc:
Display current mode and work progress within range on operation page when printer is working;
If §6§lLag Detection§r is enabled, will show prompt when lag is excessive.
litematica_printer.config.renderLayerLim: Limit printer work range to Litematica's currently rendered layer range.
litematica_printer.config.switchPrinterM: Switch printer's current work mode (printing/mining/bedrock breaking, etc.).
After pressing hotkey, record currently targeted container, and sync items from same type containers within projection selection to this container.
litematica_printer.config.syncInventoryC: When enabled, the sync first checks whether the player inventory holds all required items and skips syncing if not. Default off.
Also sync the crafter's slot disabled states when syncing (disabled states first, then items). When off, only items are synced and slot states are left untouched.
Highlight color for containers being synchronized; set to §l#00000000§r to disable highlighting.
litematica_printer.config.syncHighlightR: Maximum render distance for container sync highlights; blocks beyond this distance are not rendered. Set to 0 to disable the limit.
litematica_printer.config.updateCheck.de: Automatically check for mod updates when first entering world.
litematica_printer.config.iterationTimeL:
Maximum work time for the printer per game tick (milliseconds), covering scanning, placing and breaking.
Set to 0 to disable.
Default 8 ms balances performance and speed, adjust as needed.
litematica_printer.config.workRange.desc:
Printer's maximum work radius centered on player (blocks). Larger values mean wider coverage.
This parameter is associated with §6§lIteration Area Shape§r.
litematica_printer.config.verifierOptimi: When enabled, the schematic verifier switches to an optimized implementation: mismatches are stored in per-chunk buckets (drastically lower memory for huge schematics), scanning runs on a background thread, and all incremental updates and highlight picking are time-budgeted. Takes effect after re-entering the server.
litematica_printer.free_notice: Multilingual translation needs improvement, help us please
litematica_printer.update.available: Litematica Printer detected new version! Current version: %s, latest version: %s
litematica_printer.update.download: >> Click here to download latest version <<
litematica_printer.update.failed: Update check failed, please try again later.
litematica_printer.update.recommendation: Strongly recommend upgrading to latest version to fix potential serious issues.
When enabled, uses parallel breaking: scan collects all candidate blocks, auto-switches to the best tool, and breaks multiple blocks at once from nearest to farthest (ideal for large areas of hard blocks such as deepslate). When disabled, keeps breaking blocks one by one in order.
litematica_printer.config.breakAvoidFlui: When enabled, blocks adjacent to a fluid (lava/water) on the down, east, west, north or south face are not mined, preventing accidental breaks that release liquid. Blocks directly above a fluid are still mined. Only affects normal breaking (removing extra/wrong blocks in print mode, and the mine mode).
litematica_printer.config.breakFluidList: Blocks or items matching this list are treated as protected fluids. Supports IDs, names, pinyin and tags.
litematica_printer.config.breakAvoidSupp: When enabled, the block directly below a gravity-affected block (sand, gravel, red sand, concrete powder, anvils, dragon eggs, etc.) is not mined, preventing the supported block from falling. Only affects normal breaking.
litematica_printer.config.breakNonBlocki: When enabled, while you are manually breaking a block (holding left-click), the printer pauses its own breaking and yields the block-break state to you, preventing the player and printer from fighting over the same target. The printer resumes automatically once you stop mining. Only applies in survival/adventure; creative is unaffected.
litematica_printer.config.printCloudStor: When enabled, if a material is found missing while printing (a material required by blocks in the working range is at 0 in the inventory), all missing material types are collected and a single withdrawal order is submitted to the cloud store, entering a cooldown during which no further automatic orders are placed. The cooldown ends immediately when an ordered material arrives, letting the automatic refill resume. Requires the Cloud Store mod with its server address and login password configured.

When enabled, middle-clicking a block with a missing item in the inventory submits a withdrawal order to the cloud store (not limited by the cooldown, ordering only the clicked block's material, without starting or resetting the cooldown).

After submitting an automatic refill order, no further automatic orders are placed until the cooldown ends; the cooldown ends when the timer expires or an ordered material arrives. Middle-click ordering is not limited by the cooldown and does not start or reset this timer.
Amount of each missing material requested from the cloud store per refill.
Force Cloud Store Withdrawal on Middle Click
When enabled, middle-clicking a block no longer checks whether the item is in the inventory and directly forces a withdrawal request to the cloud store.
litematica_printer.config.printFastDirec: When enabled, the client groups targets by orientation and reuses settled views; during high-speed movement it predicts targets ahead and widens the stale-task distance moderately. No server extension protocol is used.
litematica_printer.config.printOnlyEmpty: When enabled, only shulker boxes with empty contents are selected from the inventory for placement; if no empty shulker box is available, the material is treated as missing and nothing is placed.
litematica_printer.config.printShulkerAf: When enabled, shulker box placement is deferred until all ordinary blocks (excluding water, waterlogged blocks and other shulker boxes) within the intersection of the player's interaction range and the schematic render layers are placed.
litematica_printer.config.printSkipShulk: When enabled, all shulker box placements are skipped directly (shulker boxes in the schematic are not printed, and are not counted for cloud store refill).
litematica_printer.config.placeDefaultDi: When enabled, all block placements are forced to use this direction, ignoring the actual support face. Useful for scenarios with specific orientation requirements.
litematica_printer.config.printRepairRai: When enabled, the printer checks RailShape after placing rails and will break and retry up to 3 times if neighbor updates bend them incorrectly. This is a client-side best-effort repair and cannot fix every vanilla-unstable shape.
litematica_printer.config.printBonemealC:
How many consecutive bone meal clicks to send each time a crop is processed.
Higher values grow crops faster, but also consume bone meal more aggressively.
litematica_printer.config.tweakerooAngel: When enabled, players with build permission can also pass Tweakeroo's angel block placement check. This usually affects survival mode.\nWhen disabled, Tweakeroo's original creative-only behavior is preserved.
litematica_printer.config.goTimeLimit.de:
Time budget (ms) for a single pathfinding calculation. Runs on a background thread and does not affect FPS.
Commands: /go x y z, /go <player>, /go stop.
litematica_printer.config.goMaxFall.desc: Maximum fall height (blocks) the path may walk down. Never breaks or places blocks.
litematica_printer.config.goCostLimitFac: Cost cap as a multiple of the distance lower bound from start to the nearest goal (0 = no cap, 2~32, default 8). When the smallest f (cost so far + remaining distance lower bound) exceeds bound x factor, the search declares the goal unreachable immediately instead of burning the whole time budget (shared by ghast flight and walking). Smaller = give up sooner, but may misjudge valid detours as unreachable; larger = allow longer detours.
litematica_printer.config.goHeuristicWei: Heuristic weight (1.0~10.0, default 1.0 = standard A*). The search orders nodes by f = cost so far + weight × remaining distance lower bound. At 1.0 the heuristic is admissible and the result is the shortest path under the configured cost model; raising it enables weighted A* — more greedy, locking onto a usable goal sooner within the same budget (up to about that multiple when the budget cuts the search short, still shortest when the search completes). It only affects expansion order: reachability, the cost cap and the multi-goal finish comparison still use the unweighted distance lower bound, and pruning only removes nodes that provably cannot be cheaper, so reachable goals are never misjudged as unreachable. Shared by walking and ghast flight.
litematica_printer.config.goWaypointTime: Time limit for walking to travel from the current path node to the next one = node distance × this multiplier (ticks per block, default 30, 0 = no limit). When exceeded, the current route is abandoned: scan auto-walk picks a new target and dispatches a new leg, manual /go recalculates from the current position. Pauses caused by container screens (printer refill/restock) do not count. Lowering "Auto Pathfinding - Max Speed" proportionally raises the ticks needed per block, so a small multiplier may cause false timeouts.
litematica_printer.config.goMaxSpeed.des: Maximum auto-pathfinding movement speed in blocks per second. Values above full sprint speed (~5.612) are equivalent to no limit. Default 5.7.
When enabled, pathfinding always requests sprint (equivalent to holding Ctrl); whether sprinting actually engages is decided by vanilla conditions (hunger, sneaking, collision). Overrides “Auto Pathfinding - Sprint”. Also acts as the master switch for parkour jumps (crossing gaps, including 1-block gaps): when disabled no parkour jump is allowed and paths route around gaps.
litematica_printer.config.goTakeoverView: When enabled, the client view yaw is turned toward the path direction while pathfinding (yaw only, pitch untouched). The extra offset is configured under “Auto Pathfinding - View Offset”. Note: this overrides mouse look and may interfere with printer placement rotations.
litematica_printer.config.goViewOffset.d: Additional yaw offset (degrees, integer, -180 to 180, default 0) applied on top of the path direction when taking over the view. 0 faces straight along the path; it is temporarily zeroed during parkour takeoffs and ladder/vine climbing (including jump-grabs) to preserve action heading and sprint. Only takes effect when “Auto Pathfinding - Take Over View” is enabled.
litematica_printer.config.goDeviationSto: When enabled, the distance from the player to the remaining path is checked every tick; exceeding “Auto Pathfinding - Deviation Threshold” stops the task immediately (no grace period; self-jump airborne phases are exempt). Disable to turn deviation detection off.
litematica_printer.config.goDeviationDis: Distance threshold (blocks, integer, 1-16, default 1) that triggers the deviation stop. The minimum distance to the remaining path exceeding this value stops the task: full 3D distance while on ground/in water; horizontal distance only while airborne from external forces (knockback/wash-away/falling) — otherwise the pathfinding air control would pull the player back onto the path and the deviation would never register; self-jump airborne phases (parkour/jump-up/water-jump) are exempt.
litematica_printer.config.goGhastCostOrt: Cost of one orthogonal block (up/down, forward/back, left/right), default 1. Independent of the "Walking" costs; affects route preference only, never reachability.
litematica_printer.config.goGhastCostDia: Cost of moving one block on two axes at once, default 1.414 (= √2).
Cost of moving one block on all three axes at once, default 1.732 (= √3).
litematica_printer.config.goGhastAscendM: Integer multiplier applied to the cost of any step that ascends, default 2 (the space-key ascent thrust is only half the horizontal one). Higher makes level flight preferred; 1 makes ascending cost the same as level flight.
litematica_printer.config.goGhastDescend: Integer multiplier applied to the cost of any step that descends, default 2 (same as ascending). Descending requires levelling out first and then pitching down, so it is no cheaper than climbing. Higher makes the route avoid descending; 1 makes descending cost the same as level flight.
litematica_printer.config.goGhastWallPen: Extra cost per step for cells hugging a block (3D Chebyshev distance 1), default 6, 0 = no penalty. Cells one full block away or more get no penalty. Higher values push the route further away from blocks; route preference only.
litematica_printer.config.goGhastVertLat: Each vertical step costs extra in proportion to the horizontal distance to the goal (capped at 16 blocks), default 0.2, 0 = disabled. When enabled, routes become "long level flight + altitude change near the end".
litematica_printer.config.goGhastWaypoin: Time limit for the ghast to travel from the current path node to the next one = node distance × this multiplier (ticks per block). When exceeded, the current route is abandoned: auto walk picks a new target and dispatches a new leg, manual go recalculates from the current position. 0 = no limit.
litematica_printer.config.goGhastTurnPen: Soft cost added each time the path changes direction (a step differing from the previous step). The ghast needs its body yaw to converge before flying, so every turn has a real slowdown and arc cost; higher values make routes straighter with fewer turns. Default 0, 0 = no penalty.
litematica_printer.config.goWalkCost.des: Cost of moving one block (ticks, default 20/4.317 ≈ 4.633). Falling off a ledge = this value + fall ticks; climbing out of a climbable column at the same layer = this value.
litematica_printer.config.goWalkDiagonal: Cost of one same-layer diagonal step (ticks, default 4.633 × √2 ≈ 6.552).
litematica_printer.config.goJumpUpCost.d: Cost of jumping up one block (ticks, default 4.633 + 5 = 9.633); jumping into a climbable column uses the same price. Higher makes the pathfinder avoid jumping up.
litematica_printer.config.goWaterCost.de: Cost of one block through water (ticks, default 20/2.2 ≈ 9.091); a water diagonal costs this value × √2.
litematica_printer.config.goLadderCost.d: Cost of one block up/down a ladder or vine (ticks, default 20/2.35 ≈ 8.511).
litematica_printer.config.goLadderExitCo: Cost of climbing out over the top of a ladder (jump + sidestep, ticks, default 8.511 + 4 = 12.511).
Cost of sprint-jumping across a gap (ticks, default 12, covering 2-4 block gaps). Higher makes the pathfinder avoid gaps and take detours instead.
litematica_printer.config.goSprintCost.d: Cost of one block while sprinting (ticks, default 20/5.612 ≈ 3.564): used only for the heuristic lower bound and the displayed path duration, not for any edge cost. With "Force Sprint" enabled the heuristic assumes this value.
litematica_printer.config.renderOnlyBloc: When enabled, the schematic in Litematica only renders blocks listed in "Render Blocks Only List" (including fluids and block entity visuals such as chests), and the "missing" markers of unlisted blocks are hidden as well; extra block and wrong block/state markers are unaffected and stay visible.

When "Render Blocks Only" is active, only listed blocks are rendered, one block per line; use , or ; to write multiple entries in one line. Strictly matches registry path (stone), full ID (minecraft:stone), or exact translation name; an empty list renders nothing.
litematica_printer.config.category.speci: Toggles for relaxed restrictions, unusual compatibility, and environment-dependent behavior
litematica_printer.config.eat.desc: Trigger mode: §dOff§r never eats; §dPrinter only§r eats only while the printer master switch is on; §dAny time§r eats whenever hunger reaches the threshold, regardless of the master switch. Food chain: offhand → hotbar → inventory → quick shulker boxes (if enabled); offhand food is eaten directly without switching or swapping any slot. Printing/mining/pickup/container sync are paused while eating (in-flight printer actions finish first); manual player input always wins. Blacklisted food is never eaten.
litematica_printer.config.eatHungerThres: Start eating when hunger ≤ this value (default 14 = 7 drumsticks).
litematica_printer.config.eatBlacklist.d: Food in this list is never eaten automatically. One entry per line: registry path (rotten_flesh), full ID (minecraft:rotten_flesh) or exact display name.
litematica_printer.config.eatHurtCancelC: Taking damage while eating stops eating and blocks re-triggering for this many seconds (0 = keep eating through damage).
litematica_printer.config.category.go.de: Scan auto-walk and /go pathfinding: whitelists, movement style and speed, camera and safety stops
